title: Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs instead of tags
description:
colophon's `floating-action-pin` drift check reports three actions pinned to mutable tags across `.github/workflows/`:

    actions/checkout@v4          (ci.yml, release.yml)
    actions/setup-go@v5          (ci.yml, release.yml)
    softprops/action-gh-release@v1  (release.yml)

A git tag is mutable by whoever owns the action repository. Anyone who can move `v4` can change what runs in this repo's CI without a commit here. preflag publishes release binaries from `release.yml` (and the release job has `contents: write`), so a compromised action in that job could tamper with published artifacts. That is what makes this worth closing rather than noting.

## Fix

Pin each `uses:` to the full 40-character commit SHA the tag currently resolves to, keeping the human-readable version in a trailing comment. Fleet house style:

    uses: actions/checkout@<40-char-sha> # v4.4.0

Both workflow files must be covered, not just the one colophon names — each action appears more than once.

## Acceptance criteria

- No `uses:` line in `.github/workflows/` refers to a tag or branch.
- `uv run colophon drift` (from ~/git/colophon) no longer reports `floating-action-pin` against preflag.
- Both workflow files still parse as YAML.
- SHAs are resolved from the upstream repositories, not guessed.

## Acceptance criteria

- No `uses:` line in `.github/workflows/` refers to a tag or branch.

- Both workflow files still parse as YAML.
- SHAs are resolved from the upstream repositories, not guessed.
notes:
Done, not committed (working tree carries the change).

SHAs resolved from GitHub, not guessed:

    gh api repos/actions/checkout/git/ref/tags/v4     -> commit 11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  (== tag v4.4.0)
    gh api repos/actions/setup-go/git/ref/tags/v5     -> commit 40f1582b2485089dde7abd97c1529aa768e1baff  (== tag v5.6.0)
    gh api repos/softprops/action-gh-release/git/ref/tags/v1 -> annotated tag 26994186c0ac...,
      dereferenced via git/tags/26994186c0ac... -> commit de2c0eb89ae2a093876385947365aca7b0e5f844 (== tag v0.1.15)

All five `uses:` lines across both workflow files are now SHA-pinned. No tag or branch refs remain.

Verified:
- `uv run colophon drift` no longer reports `floating-action-pin` against preflag. Only `dirty` (uncommitted, expected) and `colophon-labelled-issue` (this issue) remain.
- Both files parse: `yaml.safe_load` succeeds on ci.yml and release.yml.
- `go run github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@latest` reports zero action/workflow errors. It does emit six shellcheck info/style findings (SC2035, SC2086 x4, SC2129) inside the `run:` blocks of release.yml — all pre-existing and untouched by this change.

## Worth a follow-up

`softprops/action-gh-release@v1` resolves to v0.1.15, tagged in 2023. Upstream is on v3.0.2. Pinning to the SHA freezes the release job on that four-major-versions-old code, which is the correct behaviour-preserving move here but is not the same as being current. Bumping to v3 is a separate decision with its own input changes, so it was deliberately left out of this issue.

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text:
Follow-up: bumped action-gh-release to v3 rather than freezing at v0.1.15, per user decision.

    softprops/action-gh-release@v3 -> annotated tag c12583777ecd..., dereferenced -> commit 3d0d9888cb7fd7b750713d6e236d1fcb99157228
    v3.0.2 -> annotated tag fe965f7af51a..., dereferenced -> the same commit

So `v3` and `v3.0.2` are the same commit today; release.yml:58 pins it with a `# v3.0.2` comment.

## Input audit, v0.1.15 -> v3.0.2

Compared the two `action.yml` files directly.

**Nothing renamed. Nothing removed.** All 14 v0.1.15 inputs still exist in v3 under the same names. Five are new and additive: `make_latest`, `overwrite_files`, `preserve_order`, `previous_tag`, `working_directory`. Outputs are unchanged (`url`, `id`, `upload_url`, `assets`).

This step passes exactly two inputs, `files` and `generate_release_notes`. Both exist in v3 with unchanged semantics.

Defaults that changed: v0.1.15 defaulted only `token` (`${{ github.token }}`, still the same in v3). v3 adds defaults for the new `overwrite_files` (`true`) and `previous_tag` (`""`). `overwrite_files: true` is the one default worth naming — it is new behaviour, but this workflow creates a fresh release per pushed tag, so there are no pre-existing assets for it to act on.

The real content of the major bumps is the runtime: `using: node16` (v0.1.15) -> `node20` (v2.0.0) -> `node24` (v3.0.0). ubuntu-latest supports node24.

Two changelog entries that touch behaviour this workflow relies on, both benign here:
- 2.5.3 "prefer token input over GITHUB_TOKEN" — this step sets neither and relies on the default; the job already has `permissions: contents: write`.
- 2.5.3 tightened `files` glob handling (Windows separators, tilde expansion, escaping glob metacharacters). Every path in the `files` block is a literal — only letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.`, `/` — so no metacharacters to escape.

## Verified vs not

Verified locally: actionlint reports zero action/workflow errors, unchanged from before the bump — still only the same six pre-existing shellcheck info/style findings in release.yml `run:` blocks, none of them mine. Both files parse under `yaml.safe_load`. All five `uses:` lines are SHA-pinned. colophon drift reports no `floating-action-pin` against preflag.

**Not verified, and cannot be locally:** the release job itself. It triggers only on `push: tags: v*` on GitHub, so the v3 action has not actually executed against this workflow. The input audit says it should work; the first real proof will be the next tag push. If it fails there, `v2.6.2` is the last node20 line and a drop-in fallback.
